dial.summary: BTC holds ~$83,500 with BTC.D surging to ~59% as alts sell off and TOTAL crypto contracts to $2.85T; global M2 flat at ~$103.4T (August peak $103.66T); near-zero funding (0.01% per 8h) confirms an unlevered spot accumulation regime with BTC outperforming the broader market despite DXY at 101.36 and real yields rising to 2.90% — BTC Accumulation posture intact ahead of October 2 NFP and October 14 CPI as the next major catalysts.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at approximately $103,435B ($103.4T) as of September 28, 2026 (StreetStats/MacroMicro aggregation; 6–8 week reporting lag for official G4 data); US M2 at $23.3T in August 2026 (+5.7% YoY); 4-week trend flat: August 2026 macromicro reading $103,662B → September 28 $103,435B = −0.22% over ~4 weeks, within the <0.5% relative flat threshold; YoY still +12% (not contracting); status neutral — 4-week trend is flat rather than up (supportive requires rising trend); DXY FX conversion effect (dollar +1.5% over the period) partially explains the USD-denominated decline; October ISM (Oct 1) and NFP (Oct 2) are next macro catalysts.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1); September 2026 ISM Manufacturing releases October 1 — no official September reading available as of September 30; LEADING SIGNAL: S&P Global Flash US Manufacturing PMI for September surged to 57.0 (52-month high, released Sep 23) pointing to potential ISM upside on Oct 1; 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp on latest available official data; status neutral (above 50 but falling on 4-week basis; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 or above 62 — neither applies); a September ISM print above 55 and rising on Oct 1 would shift status to supportive.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at ~101.36 on September 29, 2026 (Fed H.15 close; up ~0.16% from prior session; heading for approximately +1.9% monthly gain in September — its strongest monthly advance since June); 4-week trend up: ~99.60 (Aug 26 per Barchart) → 101.36 (Sep 29) = +1.8% over 4 weeks, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind — DXY remains above the 100 threshold; a sustained official close below 100 required to return to neutral status; October 14 CPI is the next key DXY repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.90% as of September 28, 2026 (latest available weekday reading; up from 2.85% on Sep 25); breakeven inflation rate ~2.30%; 10Y nominal ~5.25% on Sep 29 (2Y 4.89% per Fed H.15); 4-week trend up: ~2.47% (Aug 28) → 2.90% (Sep 28) = +43bps; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); a sustained fall below 2% required to shift status to neutral/supportive; October 27–28 FOMC is the next repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 29, 2026: 10Y Treasury at 5.25%, 2Y at 4.89% (Fed H.15) → 2s10s spread = +0.36% (+36bps); 4-week trend flat: ~+38bps (Aug 26) → +36bps (Sep 29) = −2bps over 4 weeks, within the <5bps flat threshold; status neutral (positive spread but flat on 4-week basis; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); October 27–28 FOMC and October 14 CPI are the next major repricing catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,747,704M ($6.75T) for week ending September 23, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released September 24 (Treasuries $4,558B, MBS $1,910B, other $279B); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.734T (Aug 26 estimate) → $6.748T (Sep 23) = +$14B over ~4 weeks, marginal expansion within flat range; total assets up ~$140B year-on-year; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC); next H.4.1 release expected Thursday October 2.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at ~0.01% per 8h (MacroMicro September 9, 2026 reading; consistently near zero throughout September confirming an unlevered spot-driven regime); BTC spot price ~$83,517 on September 30, 2026 (CoinMarketCap), broadly flat vs prior days; TOTAL crypto $2.85T, BTC.D ~59% (surged from 56.7% over the period as alts sold off while BTC held); 30-day range consistently sub-0.01% throughout September — a classic BTC accumulation signal; status supportive (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold); Oct 2 NFP and Oct 14 CPI are next potential catalysts for a funding regime change.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$303B as of late September 2026 (StablecoinBeat tracker $302.8B; USDT ~60.6% within stablecoins, USDC ~$73.7B); total crypto market cap $2.85T (down from $2.98T prior session as alts sold off); stablecoin dominance ~10.6% ($303B / $2.85T); 30-day trend flat: dominance was ~10.4% in late August (stablecoins $309B / TOTAL $2.98T), now ~10.6% as TOTAL contracted while stablecoin cap held; status neutral — 30-day trend not clearly falling (supportive requires falling trend); headwind condition (rising dominance AND rising TOTAL) does not apply since TOTAL is falling; BTC.D ~59%, up strongly from 56.7%, suggesting BTC accumulation phase within broader alt de-risking.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Manufacturing PMI for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — the most consequential ISM read in months; August ISM was 54.6%; S&P Global Flash Manufacturing PMI surged to 57.0 (52-month high) on September 23 — a strong leading signal; a print above 55 and rising would shift the ISM indicator to supportive status; a move below 50 would signal contraction and support a shift toward Risk Off posture.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 26, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 26, 2026 — released same day as ISM Manufacturing PMI; a back-to-back rise in claims would be an early signal that cumulative rate tightening (fed funds 3.75%–4.00%) is beginning to bite on employment; prior weeks approximately 206K.

upcoming.title: Employment Situation — September 2026 NFP
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET (first Friday of October) — the most consequential pre-FOMC data release before the October 27–28 meeting; August NFP was +162K; a reading above +200K with unemployment holding sub-4.5% keeps October hike odds elevated; a surprise miss below +100K could shift the rate path significantly; watch average hourly earnings for wage inflation signals.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Services PMI for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET (first Monday of October) — the services sector accounts for ~80% of US GDP; released after post-NFP market positioning from October 2 employment data; S&P Global Flash Services PMI for September surged to 58.7 (59-month high) on September 23 — a strong leading signal for ISM Services; a print below 50 alongside a soft NFP would significantly alter the rate-path outlook ahead of October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes (September 15–16, 2026 Meeting)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the September 15–16 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET — the meeting at which the Fed raised the fed funds rate by 25bps to 3.75%–4.00%; minutes will reveal the debate around the pace of further tightening, the balance between inflation (PCE +3.7% YoY) and growth risks, and any dissents; closely watched for signals on the October 27–28 FOMC decision alongside the full October data cluster (ISM, NFP, CPI).
